biggestGap: Weapon-grip hands are single dark lumps: on all three figures the hand wrapped on the sword/axe haft shows no thumb wedge and no finger stack at panel distance, while both references show a thumb locking over wrapped fingers. The grip must read as thumb-plus-fingers, not a socket the weapon plugs into.
notes: Human fighter: reference wins. Ours reads as a bare shop-mannequin (two flat skin values, tube arms with no forearm-to-wrist taper, sword hand a single brown lump); the Valheim player's clothed torso, belt line, and separated fingers read as a person at the same poly budget. Ours does win the silhouette panel (helmet, sword, shield all legible). Orc barbarian: reference wins, but ours is the strongest of the three - real brow/tusk head, visible pec/ab value ladder, thighs rooting separately in dark trousers; the WoW grunt's mass hierarchy (boulder shoulders and forearms collapsing to a tight waist) makes our near-constant-width arms look inflated rather than muscled, and the axe-grip hand is a thumbless blob though the free left fist shows a faint knuckle ridge. Dwarf fighter: reference wins. Legs bow outward in a straddle so wide he reads as riding an invisible barrel, and the face panel has pale streaks under both eyes that read as tears at panel distance; torso banding, beard, and one-band pauldron trim seating are genuinely good. No merged-crotch fairing on any figure; feet do not overlap; pauldron trim passes. No broken panels - all six panels rendered on all three sheets, harness healthy.
